Correspondingly active_frac is null, not 0.0, and the module states plainly that null means nothing was measured; active_frac is NOT the signal. goal_state_present: false is the disambiguator the module provides: GoalState is constructed only when config.goal.z_goal_enabled is set, so z_goal is OFF in these configs -- the zero is 'disabled', not 'stepped without a writer'. Both drivers state the orthogonality in an inline comment and record the block anyway under the generous-recording standard. Conclusion: the dead-ish z_goal stream does NOT undermine either run's criteria; it is correctly recorded and correctly irrelevant here.

criterion_informativeness.reasoning: 'fires >= 1' is real content; 'need_arm_fraction == 1.0' is entailed by arm geometry -- NEED_HIGH's ceiling is 100000 in a 120-step life, so no fire CAN be ceiling-attributed. Further, the readiness precondition stimulus_crossed_threshold itself requires sleep_cycles_fired >= 1 on this same arm, so c1 substantially restates its own precondition.

Injecting a constant 1.0 against threshold 0.5 makes need_crossed() true at step 1 by arithmetic, so 'first fire 1 < 25' is close to a restatement of the injection design. CONFOUND: NEED_HIGH differs from CEILING in ceiling (100000 vs 25) as well as in MEL, so the arms differ in two ways. The confound is conservative -- a higher ceiling can only DELAY a ceiling-arm fire, never manufacture 'sooner' -- so it does not manufacture the result, but the criterion carries little information beyond what c1 already carries.

The ONLY magnitude-discriminating criterion in the whole cluster. NEED_SUB has identical wiring to NEED_HIGH and differs only in injected magnitude (0.1 vs 0.5 threshold). It discriminates between two candidate crossing statistics: under a SUM/integral, 0.1/step crosses 0.5 by step 5 and c3 FAILS; under a MEAN it never crosses. It passed -- establishing the implementation is a mean. See biological_reference.divergence for why that same result reads as a negative result under the design's own cited literature.

STRUCTURALLY UNFAILABLE. use_mel_entry=False makes MELConsumer.need_crossed() return False unconditionally (mel_consumer.py:233-234), so need_arm_fraction 0.0 / ceiling_arm_fraction 1.0 is forced. It is also a re-run of 929's c3 on a later substrate -- the same unfailable assertion stated twice across the cluster.

degenerate_regime_finding.observation: NEED_HIGH fired a sleep cycle on 120 of 120 waking steps, all three seeds, first fire at step 1.
degenerate_regime_finding.mechanism: notify_waking_step's only re-entrancy guard is _within_life_cycle_active (in-cycle only), and _run_cycle calls mel_consumer.on_cycle_complete() which RESETS the accumulator. So the next waking step re-injects 1.0, the mean is 1.0 again, and the trigger fires again. There is NO refractory period, NO hysteresis and NO minimum inter-cycle interval on the need arm; the step ceiling bounds only the MAXIMUM interval.
degenerate_regime_finding.why_it_matters: The regime is degenerate as an organism state (continuous sleep) while satisfying every pre-registered criterion, and it is precisely the regime the arm is INTENDED for -- design (b) exists to fire in a non-converging environment that sustains high MEL, which is exactly the condition producing continuous sleep here. No criterion reads fire RATE or inter-cycle interval, so the acceptance rule is blind to it.
degenerate_regime_finding.biological_reading: Not an incidental artifact of a saturating stimulus. Saper 2010's flip-flop is 'sharply bistable but intrinsically unstable' and requires an external stabiliser (orexin); MECH-286, REE's stabiliser analog, was deliberately OFF in both runs (correctly, per the synthesis -- its threat term reads a chance-level place-safety signal per V3-EXQ-917). A bistable switch run without its stabiliser is PREDICTED to chatter, and 120 transitions in 120 steps is that prediction observed. Read this way, 933 contains a positive, biology-consistent finding that its own acceptance rule discarded.

biological_reference.divergence: LOAD-BEARING, on two axes. (1) PROCESS S vs LEVEL DETECTOR. need_crossed() compares current_mel() -- MELConsumer.current_mel() == accumulator.mean(), the MEAN per-step waking PE since the last cycle -- against a fixed threshold. WakingMELAccumulator's own docstring makes the invariance deliberate: 'MEL is the MEAN per-step prediction error ... so the window length does not bias the load estimate.' Time-invariance is the RIGHT property for the role the statistic was built for (GAP-5b duration scaling: how hard was this wake window, independent of its length) and the WRONG property for the role it was reused in. Process S's defining behaviour is that constant sub-threshold demand EVENTUALLY crosses, because pressure integrates over time awake; a mean never does. The reuse route is visible in the source: need_crossed() was factored out of entry_permitted() so the GAP-9 step trigger could 'reuse the exact same crossing predicate', and the duration-consumer's scale-free semantics travelled with it into an entry-timing role where scale-freeness inverts the intended dynamic. The synthesis is explicit that design (b) IS Process S ('(b) is Process S / INV-050's third drive, and it is the best-grounded of the three'). (2) SWITCH WITHOUT STABILISER -- see degenerate_regime_finding.biological_reading.
biological_reference.divergence_is_undetectable_by_this_desig: Both runs' results are exactly what a level detector predicts and neither could have detected the divergence. NEED_HIGH (constant 1.0) crosses on step 1 and again after every reset; NEED_SUB (constant 0.1) never crosses across 120 steps. c3_threshold_gates is the SAME measurement under two opposite framings: pre-registered as 'sub-threshold demand does not spuriously fire the need arm' it PASSES; read against the design's own Process S basis -- 'does accumulated waking demand eventually reach the entry threshold?' -- the identical measurement is a NEGATIVE result (120 steps of continuous non-zero learning demand produced zero demand-driven sleep). The acceptance rule encodes only the first framing, so the run cannot arbitrate.

recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: Sleep-onset ENTRY pressure: a time-integrating demand term plus a post-fire refractory for the GAP-9 within-life trigger
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: The GAP-9 need arm (design (b)) currently fires on MELConsumer.need_crossed(), which thresholds current_mel() == accumulator.mean() -- a deliberately time-invariant statistic built for GAP-5b DURATION scaling, where scale-freeness is correct. Reused for ENTRY TIMING it inverts the intended dynamic: constant sub-threshold demand never crosses however long the agent stays awake (V3-EXQ-933 NEED_SUB: 0 need-arm fires in 120 steps), while supra-threshold demand crosses on step 1 and on every step thereafter (NEED_HIGH: 120/120 fires, no refractory). Build two things, keeping the duration statistic untouched: (i) a SEPARATE time-integrating sleep-pressure term for the entry decision (Borbely Process S -- grows with time awake, discharged by on_cycle_complete), leaving current_mel() as the duration input; (ii) a post-fire refractory / hysteresis so the bistable switch cannot chatter. The 2026-08-14 lit synthesis already names the preferred shape for the graded half (Section 5.3: route the term into MELConsumer.scale_steps()'s continuous duration factor rather than a boolean permit, degrading to current behaviour at factor 1.0). Both are `complicated (buildable)` -- no open question, no spike needed.

learning_extracted: Factoring a predicate out for reuse can silently transplant an INVARIANCE property into a role where it inverts the intended dynamic. current_mel()'s time-invariance is correct for duration scaling and wrong for entry timing; nothing at the factoring site flagged the role change. Reusable engineering lesson well beyond sleep.

The SAME measurement can pass one framing and fail another. c3_threshold_gates is a PASS as 'threshold gating works' and a negative result as 'does accumulated demand eventually cross?'. Where a criterion is genuinely two-sided, declare BOTH directions in the interpretation grid rather than pre-registering only the favourable one.

A saturated arm is not a validated arm: firing on 120 of 120 waking steps satisfied every criterion while demonstrating the trigger has no minimum inter-cycle interval. A diagnostic validating a TRIGGER should carry a degeneracy guard on the fire RATE, not only on the fire COUNT.

A deliberately-disabled dependency still shapes the result and should be read for its predicted signature. MECH-286 (the orexin/stabiliser analog) was correctly OFF, and the chattering flip-flop that produced is exactly what Saper 2010 predicts for a bistable switch without its external stabiliser -- a positive, biology-consistent finding the acceptance rule discarded.

Arm geometry can entail a criterion as surely as a wiring flag can: NEED_HIGH's 100000 ceiling in a 120-step life makes 'every fire is the need arm' unfailable, and the c2 comparison is confounded by that same geometry (conservatively, but confounded).

Recording debt again: cycle_history's merged per-fire metrics existed at run time and were discarded, so 'did the fired cycle do any consolidation work?' is unanswerable from the manifest at ~1.5 s of spent compute.

The convergent property is that the composed trigger has been validated twice against the CONNECTIVITY half of its specification and never once against the DYNAMICS half -- inter-cycle interval, time-to-cross under sustained demand, demand-proportionality of onset -- which is precisely the half that distinguishes the Process-S accumulator the design brief specified from the level detector that was built.
